full_text_en:
Guiding Case No. 237

Langxi Certain Service Outsourcing Co., Ltd. v. Xu Moushen — dispute over confirmation of labor relationship

(Discussed and adopted by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, issued on December 20, 2024)

Keywords Civil; confirmation of labor relationship; new forms of employment; contracting and cooperation agreements; actual performance; labor management

Ruling Gist

Where a platform enterprise or a platform employment cooperation enterprise enters into a contracting or cooperation agreement with a worker, and the worker claims that a labor relationship exists with the enterprise, the people's court shall, based on the employment facts, comprehensively consider factors such as the degree of the worker's autonomy in deciding working hours and workload, the degree of management and control over the labor process, whether the worker is required to comply with relevant work rules, algorithm rules, labor discipline, and reward and punishment measures, the continuity of the worker's work, and whether the worker can decide or change transaction prices, and make a corresponding determination in accordance with the law. Where employment facts exist and constitute dominant labor management, a labor relationship shall be determined to exist in accordance with the law.

Basic Facts

Langxi Certain Service Outsourcing Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Langxi Service Company) and the operator of a certain "DongMaicai" (vegetable delivery) platform, Shanghai Certain Network Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shanghai Network Company), entered into a "Service Contracting Agreement" on April 1, 2019. The agreement stipulated that: Langxi Service Company would complete tasks such as sorting and delivering goods for Shanghai Network Company; the parties would regularly reconcile the contracting fees for the previous month each month, after which Shanghai Network Company would make payment; Langxi Service Company would manage the personnel providing services itself and independently bear the corresponding remuneration, commercial insurance premiums, welfare benefits, and employer liability or other liabilities as provided by laws and regulations.

In July 2019, Langxi Service Company arranged for Xu Moushen to engage in delivery work at a Jiuting station of the DongMaicai platform. Langxi Service Company entered into a "Freelancer Cooperation Agreement" and a "New Format Freelancer Task Contracting Agreement" with Xu Moushen. Both agreements stipulated that: Xu Moushen and Langxi Service Company established a cooperative relationship, and their relationship was not subject to the Labor Contract Law. Among them, the "New Format Freelancer Task Contracting Agreement" stipulated that: Langxi Service Company would pay service fees to Xu Moushen in accordance with the service standards and fee standards for project service personnel confirmed by the cooperating company; there was no base salary or guaranteed service fee, and the system was "more work, more pay; less work, less pay." However, Langxi Service Company did not pay fees according to the service fee calculation method agreed in the above agreements; the remuneration actually paid to Xu Moushen included items such as basic remuneration, per-order remuneration, and bonuses. On August 12, 2019, Langxi Service Company transferred RMB 9,042.74 (currency unit: RMB, hereinafter the same) to Xu Moushen. On August 13, 2019, Xu Moushen, following instructions at the station to build a wooden frame, accidentally injured his right foot while cutting木板 (wooden boards). He was hospitalized for treatment and did not continue working at that station thereafter. On September 3, 2019, Langxi Service Company paid Xu Moushen RMB 15,000 under the name "service fee." During Xu Moushen's work at the station, his attendance time was relatively fixed; he was subject to station management, clocked in for work according to the shift schedule, completed delivery tasks according to system assignments, and when there were no delivery tasks, he performed miscellaneous chores at the station.

Xu Moushen, due to a dispute with Langxi Service Company over the determination of a work-related injury, applied for labor arbitration. The Songjiang District Labor Personnel Dispute Arbitration Commission of Shanghai ruled that a labor relationship existed between Xu Moushen and Langxi Service Company from July 5, 2019, to August 13, 2019. Langxi Service Company disagreed and filed a lawsuit with the Songjiang District People's Court of Shanghai.

Judgment

The Songjiang District People's Court of Shanghai rendered a civil judgment on July 5, 2021, (2021) Hu 0117 Min Chu No. 600: confirming that a labor relationship existed between Xu Moushen and Langxi Certain Service Outsourcing Co., Ltd. from July 5, 2019, to August 13, 2019. After the judgment was pronounced, Langxi Certain Service Outsourcing Co., Ltd. disagreed and filed an appeal. The Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court rendered a civil judgment on March 7, 2022, (2021) Hu 01 Min Zhong No. 11591: rejecting the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

Reasoning

The focus of the dispute in this case is: given that Langxi Service Company and Xu Moushen entered into a contracting and cooperation agreement, whether and how to determine that a labor relationship exists between the two parties.

Whether a labor relationship exists has a significant impact on the rights and interests of the worker. Where a labor relationship exists, the worker is legally entitled to a series of rights such as obtaining labor remuneration, enjoying social insurance and welfare, and receiving economic compensation and damages, and also bears obligations such as accepting the management of the employing unit. According to the provisions of the Labor Law of the People's Republic of China and the Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China: "An employing unit establishes a labor relationship with a worker from the date of employment" and "a labor contract shall be concluded when establishing a labor relationship." However, in practice, there are situations where enterprises enter into contracts such as contracting or cooperation agreements with workers to avoid establishing labor relationships with them. In this regard, the people's court shall, based on the employment facts, comprehensively consider factors such as personality subordination, economic subordination, and organizational subordination, accurately determine whether a labor relationship exists between the enterprise and the worker, and handle cases concerning the protection of labor rights and interests in accordance with the law. Article 1 of the "Notice of the Ministry of Labor and Social Security on Certain Issues Concerning the Establishment of Labor Relations" (Lao She Bu Fa [2005] No. 12) stipulates: "Where an employing unit recruits a worker without concluding a written labor contract, but the following circumstances exist simultaneously, the labor relationship is established: (1) the employing unit and the worker meet the subject qualifications prescribed by laws and regulations; (2) the various labor rules and regulations formulated by the employing unit in accordance with the law apply to the worker, the worker is subject to the labor management of the employing unit, and engages in paid labor arranged by the employing unit; (3) the labor provided by the worker constitutes a component of the employing unit's business." It can be seen that the essential characteristic of a labor relationship is dominant labor management. Under the new employment format, the production and operation methods of platform enterprises have undergone significant changes, and the specific forms of labor management have also acquired many new characteristics. However, the determination of a labor relationship should still comprehensively consider the presence and strength of personality subordination, economic subordination, and organizational subordination. Specifically, it should comprehensively consider factors such as the degree of the worker's autonomy in deciding working hours and workload, the degree of management and control over the labor process, whether the worker is required to comply with relevant work rules, algorithm rules, labor discipline, and reward and punishment measures, the continuity of the worker's work, and whether the worker can decide or change transaction prices, and make a corresponding determination in accordance with the law.

In this case, although Langxi Service Company and Xu Moushen entered into a contracting and cooperation agreement, according to relevant legal provisions and in light of the facts ascertained by the court, it should be determined that a labor relationship existed between Xu Moushen and Langxi Service Company. Specifically: First, Xu Moushen engaged in delivery work at the station, was subject to station management, clocked in for work according to the station's shift schedule, and completed delivery tasks on time according to assignments. He could not independently choose delivery times or tasks, and even when there were no delivery tasks, he was required to stay at the station to perform chores. Second, Xu Moushen's remuneration composition included items such as basic remuneration, per-order remuneration, and bonuses, indicating that Langxi Service Company conducted corresponding assessment and management of Xu Moushen's work and paid remuneration accordingly. Third, Langxi Service Company undertook tasks such as sorting and delivering goods from Shanghai Network Company, and the delivery work performed by Xu Moushen constituted an important component of the business undertaken by Langxi Service Company. In summary, employment facts existed between Xu Moushen and Langxi Service Company, constituting dominant labor management, which conforms to the essential characteristics of a labor relationship, and a labor relationship should be determined to exist.

Related Legal Provisions

Article 16 of the Labor Law of the People's Republic of China

Articles 7 and 10 of the Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China
